page.layout: One printed page. At top, two coin engravings side by side, each with a legend around its rim. Below them, one column of running text with two entries and two italic quotations. At the foot, a decorative ornament. No margin notes.

main_text.l: SIBYLLA Europa, siue Europea, vulgò vndecima inter
Sibyllas, hoc est fatidicas, & Deo plenas, confiliíque diuini
participes mulieres annumeratur. De hac non memini me vs-
quam quidquam apud autores legisse, nisi quòd libellus ille
vetus, qui de Sibyllarum vaticiniis est, Sibyllæ huic hanc tri-

l.i: Veniet ille, & transfibit montes & colles, & latices Syluarum olympi:
regnabit in paupertate, & dominabitur in silentio: & egredietur de vte-

main_text.l: SIBYLLA Ægyptia, quam supradictus libellus Sibyllam
Agrippa vocat, ab Æliano inter quatuor Sibyllas enumeratur:
quæ sunt hoc ordine, Erythræa, Samia, Ægyptia, & Sardiana.
Sibyllas porrò in iis quæ de Christo, aut aliis ad humanā salu-
tem spectatibus, sunt vaticinatæ, probabile habet D. Augu.(seu
bonæ fuerint seu malæ) à Deo edoctas fuisse: nā prophetiæ do-
num bonis esse commune ac malis. Vide S. August. de ciui. Dei
li.18.ca.23. & Cæl. Rhodig. li.21.ca.37. nec me fugit de quadam
Sibylla mentionem fecisse Diod.Sicu.lib.5. Huius Ægyptiæ Si-

l.i: Inuisibile verbum palpabitur, & germinabit ut radix, & siccabitur
ut folium, & non apparebit venustas eius. &c.

page.notes: Coin legends, not transcribed as text: left coin "SIBYLLA" (partly visible, reads SIB...) and "EVROPA" running around the rim; right coin "SIBYLLA" (partly visible) and "AEGYPTA" around the rim. The legends are part of the engravings. Bottom ornament is a decorative woodcut fleuron with no text. The "Augu." abbreviation is followed by a mark where the printed name "Augustinus" is abbreviated; transcribed as printed. "August." is printed with long s, transcribed with plain s as required.
